newsitem.title: LATVIA: REUTERS BALTIC NEWS - MARKETS WHILE YOU SLEPT.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS BALTIC NEWS - MARKETS WHILE YOU SLEPT.

text.p: These are the main developments on markets overnight:

NEW-YORK. A late session bout of bargain hunting lifted U.S. stocks on Monday. Dow registered a rise of 108.07 points, or 1.4 percent, to 7,803.36, regaining almost half of Friday's 247-point decline.

TOKYO. Shares shed most of their gains to trade just slightly higher in the early afternoon on Tuesday, as participants were discouraged by the market's own weak recovery after New York rebounded strongly.
At 0427 GMT, the 225-share Nikkey average was up 33.91 points or 0.18 percent at 19,075.01.
LONDON. FTSE 100 ended 0.6 percent lower on Monday as Wall Street retreated after initial bounce. Firm T-bills, bonds also lend support.
Dollar was slightly firmer against yen on light short-covering by interbank dealers in afternoon Tokyo but remained top-heavy amid exporter offers near 118.50 yen.
Mark also edged up against yen, which also indirectly supported greenback versus yen.
Among today's economic indicators, there are U.S. July housing start numbers at 1230 GMT and U.S. July import and export prices at 1400 GMT.
